This appeal has been directed against the judgment dated 29th August, 2023 passed in CWP No.
1612 of 2023 titled Banasar Ram and Ors vs. State of HP & others, whereby direction has been State Of Hp & Ors vs Banasar Ram & Ors on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42524437/

sentences.text: "Consequently, in view of the detailed discussion made herein above as well as law taken into consideration, this Court finds merit in the present petition and accordingly same is allowed with direction to the respondents to initiate acquisition proceedings within four weeks under the relevant statute vis-a-vis land of the petitioners and thereafter, just and fair compensation qua the same be awarded to the petitioners.

Since petitioners have been fighting for their rightful claim for so long, this Court hopes and trusts that authority concerned .
would do the needful expeditiously preferably, within two months."

2. Undisputedly land belonging to the petitioner has been utilized by the State for constructing a link road Jarol Khai Ghat via Behna under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojna but no compensation was paid to the petitioner.

It has been recorded in the impugned judgment that vide Notification dated 11.10.2018, issued under Section 4 of Land Acquisition Act 1894, Khasra Numbers adjoining to the land of the appellants were acquired by the State but land belonging to the appellants was not acquired.
3. In this appeal, main ground for assailing the judgment is that claim of the land owners was liable to be rejected for delay and latches on their part.
4 We have heard learned Additional Advocate General and have also gone through the judgment passed on 29th August, 2023 in CWP No. 1612 of 2023.

5 These grounds have been considered and dealt with by learned Single Judge in the light of judgments passed by the Supreme Court in State of Himachal Pradesh vs. Umed Ram Sharma (1986)2 SCC 468; State of Maharashtra vs.Digambar (1995)4 SCC 683; Vidya Devi vs. State of HP and others (2020)2 SCC 569; Hari Krishana Mandir Trust vs. State of Maharashtra & others (2020)9 SCC 356;
Sukh Dutt Ratra and another vs. State of Himachal Pradesh and .
others (2022)7 SCC 508; Civil Appeal No. 1278 of 2023 titled State of Himachal Pradesh vs. Rajiv and another, decided on 24.2.2023 as well as judgments passed by this High Court on 18.7.2023 in CWP No. 8647 of 2022 titled as Ramanand and others vs. State of HP and others; dated 27.7.2023 passed in CWP No. 5928 of 2022 titled Vir Sain vs. State of HP and others and in Shankar Dass vs.
State of Himachal Pradesh, CWP No. 1966 of 2010 decided on 2.3.2013, has allowed the petition.

sentences.text: 7 Learned Additional Advocate General is not able to point out any ground indicating that present case is not squarely covered by aforesaid verdicts of the Court.

. 
8 In aforesaid facts and circumstances, we do not find any illegality, irregularity or any other perversity in the impugned judgment.
Therefore, appeal is liable to be dismissed being devoid of merits.
9 We consider it fit to record that State is preferring the appeals despite dismissal of their similar appeals in identical matters.
Such conduct is not in consonance with the Litigation Policy adopted by the State of HP which is causing wasting the time and energy of the State as well as the Court.
It may invite imposing cost but taking lenient view, no cost is being imposed.
10. Accordingly, appeal is dismissed with direction that consequential action, in terms of judgment dated 29.08.2023 passed in CWP No. 1612 of 2023 be taken within four weeks.
Appeal stands disposed of along with all pending miscellaneous application(s), if any.

(Vivek Singh Thakur) (Judge) (Ranjan Sharma) Judge 15th June, 2024 (veena)
